title: Migrations apply in order, each inside a single transaction; a mid-migration crash leaves the store on the previous version
description: The migration runner iterates pending migrations in ascending version order. For each migration, the runner opens a transaction, executes every statement in the migration, writes the version row into the bookkeeping table, and commits. A failure at any step aborts the transaction and rolls back; the on-disk version reflects the last successfully committed migration. The runner surfaces the failure with a specific error code naming the version that failed.
rationale: Half-applied migrations are the shape that turns a schema evolution into a hand-recovery incident. Wrapping each migration in one transaction with its version bump means the store is always at a version the code knows how to interpret. Naming the failing version in the error means the operator can inspect the exact statement set that failed.
